summary: The TCP authority ledger has ONE record per resource-hash slot (MXFS_TAUTH_SLOTS=65536, page=slot/31). Two live INODE resources whose hashes collide cannot both be recorded: the second grant is refused -EEXIST at the ledger (tauth_ledger.c ~644 P-TAUTH-COLLISION, fail closed), the master denies MXFS_ERR_LEDGER, and the requester turns that into -EIO to the file operation (dlm.c ~3452 'if (ret > 0) return -EIO'). With 8000 live inodes in the s429 workload the birthday bound makes collisions certain (44 seen); a production filesystem with millions of live inodes would refuse a large fraction of inode locks. The refusal is correct fail-closed behaviour for the record; the DESIGN cannot serve more distinct live resources than slots, and the caller sees a hard EIO rather than a wait.
mechanism: By construction (sess422 step 3 design, docs/tcp-authority-ledger.md): mxfs_tauth_ledger_slot(res) = resource_hash_raw % 65536; apply_op GRANT on a slot whose ACTIVE record names a different resource returns -EEXIST (l->collisions++). dlm_promote_txn: rc -EEXIST -> it->rc=-EEXIST -> deliver sends MXFS_MSG_LOCK_DENY status MXFS_ERR_LEDGER; requester dlm_lock_impl: any deny status other than REMASTER/LEDGER_BUSY -> return -EIO (no retry: the collision persists as long as the other holder lives). The CAW transport has the same 65536-slot table (MXFS_CAW_MAX_SLOTS) but its slot semantics differ (per-slot waiter bits; D-SAMENODE-WAITER-CANCEL-COLLISION covers its own collision class).
